question: In a future fusion reactor operating on the Deuterium-Tritium (D-T) cycle, the reaction is: $^2_1H + ^3_1H \rightarrow ^4_2He + n + 17.6 \text{ MeV}$. If the reactor must provide a steady output of $10^{15} \text{ Joules}$ of energy per year, what is the minimum combined mass of Deuterium and Tritium fuel required for one year of continuous operation? (Assume $1 \text{ MeV} = 1.6 \times 10^{-13} \text{ J}$ and average mass of fuel pair $\approx 5.0 \text{ g/mol}$).
